data.name: Sandor
data.gender_notes: Sandor is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Originally a Hungarian name, Sandor is derived from the Old Hungarian word 'sand' meaning 'defender' and 'or' meaning 'man'. In Christian tradition, Sandor is associated with the biblical figure of Saint Dorothy, who was a defender of her faith and miraculously protected by a palm tree during a Roman persecution. The name Sandor carries the meaning “Defender of mankind” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sandor usually hope their child will grow to embody defender of mankind and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Sandor belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Defender of mankind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sandor total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם שנדור הוא שינוי של השם אלכסנדרוס, שפירושו מגן ומגין, ומשמש כהגנה וכחוסן לאדם שנושא אותו. השם נמצא בשימוש בקרב יהודים ונוצרים כאחד, ויש לו קונוטציות של כוח והגנה.

in_greek.name: Σάνδορ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Σάνδορ είναι μια παραλλαγή του ονόματος Αλέξανδρος, που σημαίνει προστάτης και υπερασπιστής. Στην παράδοση των Ανατολικών Ορθοδόξων Εκκλησιών, το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια της προστασίας και της υπεράσπισης, και συχνά αποδίδεται σε πρόσωπα που κατέχουν θέση ευθύνης και προστασίας.

in_latin.name: Sandor
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Sandor derivatur ex nomine Alexandrus, quod significat protector et defensor. In traditione Christiana, nomen Sandor habet connotationem protectionis et defensionis, et saepe attribuitur personis quae habent positionem auctoritatis et protectionis.

in_english.name: Sandor
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sandor is a variant of Alexander, derived from the Greek words 'alexein' meaning 'to defend' and 'andros' meaning 'man'. It signifies a defender or protector of the people. Historically, the name has been associated with Saint Alexander, a 3rd-century bishop of Jerusalem. In Christian tradition, Sandor embodies the virtues of courage, leadership, and protection. It is popular across various cultures, symbolizing strength and guardianship.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sandor has been popular in Hungarian culture for centuries. It is a powerful name that conveys strength, courage, and protection. Hungarian folklore features many legendary Sandors who defended their people against invading armies or mythical beasts. The name Sandor continues to be widely used in Hungary and other parts of the world with Hungarian communities.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, Sandor is a name that resonates with the strength and courage that comes from standing up for one's beliefs. It is a reminder of the power of faith and the importance of remaining steadfast in the face of adversity. The Saint Dorothy connection adds an additional layer of meaning, as her story serves as an inspiration for those who are called to defend their faith and values, even in the face of persecution. The name Sandor, then, can be seen as a symbol of spiritual resilience and unwavering commitment to one's beliefs.
